___ with heart failure (unknown EF, no echo in our system), 
pneumonia currently on antibiotics and recent fall ___ days ago 
at her nursing home who presents with a distal femur fracture.

She had mechanical fall in the bathroom at her nursing home 
approximately 18 days ago, with lower extremity pain and 
difficulty ambulating.

She has had persistent pain since then 
and knew "something was wrong." She was able to move her right 
lower extremity until approx. 6 days ago, when limb movement 
became difficult ___ worsening pain.
She was evaluated at

___ 1 day PTA where plain radiographs of 
the lower extremity showed a mildly angulated, mildly displaced
R distal femoral fracture.

Patient presented to the ___ ED 
accompanied by her daughters for further care.

Patient underwent multiple plain films but was having continued 
lower extremity pain and difficulty ambulating underwent femur 
film which showed fracture.

She is brought in from the nursing 
home by her daughters.

They report she is at her baseline mental 
status.
In the ED, initial vitals: T 98.1 P 72 BP 129/73 RR 18 SpO2 95%
RA
- Exam notable for:
- Labs notable for:  WBC 14 with 72.5% PMN, normal UA, normal

- Imaging notable for: CXR with left base opacity c/f PNA and 
possible effusion, plain films of pelvis, femur, knees with R 
distal femur fracture.

Ortho evaluated patient and determined 
she will likely need ORIF once medically clear.
- Patient given: CTX 1gmx1, losartan 100mg x1, fentanyl 75mcg,
APAP 1000mg x1
- Vitals prior to transfer:  P 79 BP 112/72 RR 18 SpO2 95% RA

On arrival to the floor, pt reports feeling "good" and not in 
pain.
Endorses cough.

She denies SOB, CP, fevers/chills, 
dysuria, diarrhea, constipation, new skin rashes or lesions.

Of note, she has been having a productive cough has been on a 
course of ceftriaxone, levofloxacin for PNA.

She reports full 
compliance with all medications while at the nursing home.

ACTIVE ISSUES
# RIGHT FEMUR FRACTURE
Ms. ___ suffered a fall over 2 weeks prior to presentation.

She 
had persistent pain and difficulty ambulating and persistent 
bruising after the fall and was brought in by her daughters for 
further evaluation.

Plain radiographs of the pelvis and both 
femurs revealed a mildly angulated, displaced fracture of the 
right distal femur.

She was evaluated by orthopedic surgery, who 
offered operative management.

Given her goals, and desire to 
avoid an operation, surgery was deferred and non-operative 
management was pursued.

The right leg was immobilized and she 
was started on medication for pain control with standing
Tylenol.
She declined any further pain medication.

She was 
evaluated by physical therapy ___
# PNA, LUNG MASS

Ms. ___ was diagnosed with a pneumonia and was on ceftriaxone 
and Levaquin prior to admission.

A CXR on admission showed left 
lung base consolidation, possible pleural effusion, and a 
density in the right lung.
Review of recent chest CT from

___ showed 17mm spiculated mass in her right upper lobe 
corresponding to density on CXR.
She was on vancomycin/ceftazidime for

HCAP coverage while inpatient and switched to PO levofloxacin on 
discharge for total 7-day course (due to end on ___.
CHRONIC ISSUES
# CHF: Patient had a reported history of CHF with an unknown EF
(no ECHO on ___ OMR).

She was continued on her home 
furosemide.

# Afib: Patient was continued on home Coumadin for a target INR 
of ___.

She remained in this therapeutic range throughout her 
hospitalization.

She was also continued on her home propranolol 
at 80mg TID, with good rate control.

She remained in afib 
throughout her hospitalization.

Please see anticoagulation sheet 
for further details regarding her dosing and INR.

# HTN: Losartan was held on admission and SBPs were 110s-130s so 
it was held on discharge.
Consider re-starting if hypertensive.
# HLD: Patient's statin was discontinued.
